nodes.description: A second cytosolic DNA sensor, the AIM2 inflammasome, contributes to the joint disease. In the DNase II-deficient mouse, loss of AIM2 reduces joint inflammation and caspase-1 activation while leaving the systemic inflammation AIM2-independent, so AIM2 is modeled as a tissue-specific contributor to the arthropathy rather than a driver of the whole syndrome. Its role in human DNASE2 deficiency is inferred from the mouse.

nodes.description: Biallelic DNASE2 variants abolish or sharply reduce the activity of DNase II, a lysosomal acid endonuclease. In the index families the missense and exon 4-skipping alleles left little or no measurable activity against plasmid DNA when expressed in HEK293T cells, and patient fibroblast lysates had markedly reduced activity that wild-type DNASE2 restored. This is the lysosomal-hydrolase substitution at the trigger node of the lysosomal substrate accumulation module; the stored substrate is DNA.

nodes.description: Removing the type I interferon receptor rescues the embryonic lethality, and the surviving mice develop a chronic TNF-dependent polyarthritis resembling rheumatoid arthritis, with cytopenia, extramedullary hematopoiesis and liver fibrosis. This model captures the postnatal interferon-independent inflammatory arm, including the arthropathy.

Constitutive DNase II-null mice die in late embryogenesis or at birth from a severe anemia, because macrophages at the site of fetal liver definitive erythropoiesis cannot digest the nuclei expelled by erythroid precursors. The model reproduces the macrophage DNA accumulation and the lethal fetal anemia but not the full postnatal human syndrome, which is only seen once the embryonic lethality is bypassed.

Accumulated self DNA also breaks B-cell tolerance. Patients develop fluctuating anti-DNA antibodies, and some develop a lupus-like picture with antinuclear antibodies and hypocomplementemia. In the DNase II-deficient mouse this autoantibody arm depends on the endosomal TLR chaperone Unc93b1 rather than on STING, so it is modeled as a separate route from the self DNA rather than as a consequence of the interferon node.

nodes.description: STING signaling also drives an interferon-independent proinflammatory cytokine arm. In patients the serum cytokine pattern overlaps that of STING gain-of-function disease, with raised TNF-alpha and variable IL-1beta and IL-6. Mouse work shows this arm runs through TBK1 recruitment to STING and NF-kB rather than through IRF3 and type I interferon: a STING mutant that cannot induce interferon still causes TNF- and IL-6-dependent polyarthritis. This arm is the likely driver of the deforming arthropathy.

nodes.description: Macrophages at sites of definitive erythropoiesis (fetal liver Kupffer cells, bone marrow macrophages) and at sites of developmental apoptosis engulf expelled erythroid nuclei and apoptotic cells but cannot digest their chromatin, which accumulates as undigested DNA in their lysosomes. Unlike the classical lysosomal storage diseases, the damage that follows is driven by innate immune sensing of the stored DNA rather than by storage cytotoxicity, so this entry conforms only to the first two nodes of the lysosomal module.

nodes.description: DNA that escapes lysosomal degradation is detected by cGAS, which synthesizes cGAMP and activates STING. This is the DNASE2-specific substitution at the module's entry node: the DNA reaches cGAS from a failed lysosomal digestion rather than from loss of a cytosolic nuclease such as TREX1. The route by which lysosomal DNA reaches cytosolic cGAS is not established in the cited sources. The pathway dependence is shown genetically in mice: cGAMP accumulates in DNase II-deficient tissues in a cGAS-dependent way, and deleting cGas or Sting rescues both the embryonic lethality and the arthritis.
nodes.id: cGAS-STING Activation by Undegraded Self DNA
